angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 1,000,315 km at 44.83 pc = 0.3 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 22.3056 +/- 0.0218 mas (same row, RUWE 0.92): 44.83 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.438 (1.409 to 1.467) from Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26; astrophysical_parameters of the same source): 1,000,315 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.083 (1.043 to 1.123) from Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26; astrophysical_parameters of the same source); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5961 +/- 1.4 K from Andrae et al. (2023), A&A 674, A27 (Gaia DR3 GSP-Phot), astrophysical_parameters of Gaia DR3 297045096447719040: teff_gspphot 5960.836 K (16th-84th percentiles 5959.5176-5962.296), the temperature FLAME used (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202243462). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Andrae et al. (2023), A&A 674, A27 (Gaia DR3 GSP-Phot), astrophysical_parameters of Gaia DR3 297045096447719040: teff_gspphot 5960.836 K (16th-84th percentiles 5959.5176-5962.296), the temperature FLAME used (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202243462)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/belenos.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.157, rounded to two decimals
